review: 2:3 לְכִסֵּא חֶסֶד אַדִּיר — the Arabic لِعَرْشِ نِعْمَةِ الْقَوِيّ is Heb 4:16 (כִּסֵּא הֶחָסֶד); the Hebrew keeps the construct and the adjective, so the throne is named by the attribute the epistle names, rather than by 'the mighty One's throne'.

3:1–2 הִיא קְטֹרֶת עוֹלָה בְּהֵיכַל קָדְשֶׁךָ — the Arabic هِيَ بَخُورٌ صَاعِدٌ فِي هَيْكَلِ الْقُدْسِ is Ps 141:2 (תִּכּוֹן תְּפִלָּתִי קְטֹרֶת) with Rev 8:3–4; קְטֹרֶת is kept as the cultic noun and the temple is the sanctuary, so prayer is described in the vocabulary of the incense service and not as a metaphor of smell alone.

3:3–4 הַזֶּבַח אֲשֶׁר תַּקְרִיב נַפְשִׁי — the Arabic الذَّبِيحَةُ الَّتِي تَرْفَعُهَا نَفْسِي is 'the sacrifice which my soul lifts'; זֶבַח and the Hiphil of קָרַב are kept together, since the Arabic has both the victim and the offering-up, and Hebrew needs both nouns to say it.

4:1–2 יָרִיחַ … וְרֵיחָהּ כַּצָּרִי — the Arabic يَشْتَمُّهَا … وَعَرْفُهَا كَالطِّيب is the sacrifice-of-pleasant-odour language (Gen 8:21, רֵיחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ); the Hebrew keeps the verb of smelling, which is the bold part of the stanza, rather than softening it to 'accepts it'.

5:3–4 גּוֹבֶרֶת … וּמְבִיאָה שָׁלוֹם — the Arabic تَغْلِبُ فِي جِهَادِهَا … وَتُوجِدُ السَّلَام is 'triumphs in its struggle … and brings peace into being'; the Hebrew uses גָּבַר (Exod 17:11, וְגָבַר יִשְׂרָאֵל) so the victory is the same verb as Israel's victory while Moses prays — which is the stanza's argument.
